M_T1_COMPONENTWISE_CONE_DOMINANCE.statement: If candidate d satisfies A_d>=A_e and I_d>=I_e for every e!=d, with at least one strict inequality for each competitor, then every frozen grammar uniquely selects d.
M_T1_COMPONENTWISE_CONE_DOMINANCE.proof: Each frozen endpoint functional has F_g=alpha_g*A+beta_g*I with alpha_g>0 and beta_g>0 from raw-history enumeration. Therefore F_g(d)-F_g(e)=alpha_g*(A_d-A_e)+beta_g*(I_d-I_e)>0 for every e.
M_T1_COMPONENTWISE_CONE_DOMINANCE.scope: frozen six-grammar registry and any additional grammar whose enumerated launch/incidence endpoint coefficients are both strictly positive

M_T2_ENDPOINT_FUNCTIONAL_EQUIVALENCE.statement: If two microgrammars induce identical endpoint functional F(A,I) for every seed pair, then for every six-candidate state they produce identical endpoint B vector and identical count-mode output/unresolved status, regardless of different internal history organization.
M_T2_ENDPOINT_FUNCTIONAL_EQUIVALENCE.instantiation: G1, G2 and G5 all enumerate unit coefficients (1,2), hence B=A+2I identically; G1 internal P/Q state swap is a conjugacy preserving the same history count.

M_T3_DEPENDENCE_CERTIFICATE.statement: Grammar-independent endpoint-count canonicality fails on the declared registry because G4 can reverse a strict ordering selected by G0/G1/G2/G3/G5.
M_T3_DEPENDENCE_CERTIFICATE.compact_certificate: A=(0,1,0,0,0,0), I=(1,0,0,0,0,0): G0/G1/G2/G3/G5 uniquely select 0 while G4 uniquely selects 1.

interpretation: dependency is caused by different raw-history multiplicities of the same launch/incidence source classes, not by arbitrary weights or candidate-specific grammar
